# Vadim Sokolov

> The website of Vadim Sokolov: research, teaching and books. The books are free to read, and each one has a page with its description and how to cite it. A book with results also has a page with its results and their numbers.

Each book has a Markdown page with its description and how to cite it. A book with results also has its main results on that page and a Markdown page with all its results by chapter with their numbers. A summary of each chapter is linked under the book. The full text is the PDF and the source on GitHub, under CC BY 4.0. To prove, check or extend a result of a book that has results, start with the catalog that is linked under that book: it lists every result with its status, including the open and conditional ones. When you use a result, cite the book and the number of the result.

## P = RP: A Monte Carlo Program for P versus NP

To prove, check or extend a result of this book, start with its catalog: each of the 47 results has its exact statement, its status (proved, conditional or open), its assumptions, its origin, its printed number and page, and the LaTeX file of its source. The numbers and pages are those of version 1.0.0 of the PDF. Cite the book and the number of the result.

- [P = RP: A Monte Carlo Program for P versus NP](https://vsokolov.org/books/p_equals_rp/index.html.md): by Nick Polson and Vadim Sokolov (2026). N queens counting as a rare event and a quantile integral, turned into a Monte Carlo program for P versus NP: NP = RP is shown equivalent to sampling queens completions, promise RP = promise P, which implies P = RP, is restated as a hitting set problem, with exact computations on the queens. Keywords: P versus NP, randomized complexity, RP, N queens problem, approximate counting, Monte Carlo, vertical likelihood, nested sampling, Lorenz curve, rare event simulation, Markov chain mixing, derandomization.
- [How to cite](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23738431): DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23738431 for version 1.0.0 (10.5281/zenodo.23738430 for all versions); the BibTeX entry is on the book page
- [Results by chapter](https://vsokolov.org/books/p_equals_rp/results.html.md): 47 results with their statements, status and numbers
- [Catalog of results](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/p_equals_rp/main/RESULTS.md): 47 results with their statements, status and printed numbers
- [Catalog as data](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/p_equals_rp/main/results.yaml): the same results as YAML, each with id, label, name, chapter, origin, status, conditions, summary and statement
- [All facts as JSON](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/p_equals_rp/main/site/book.json): title, authors, DOIs, licenses, links, citation, chapters with summaries, and every result with its printed number, page, source file and LaTeX label
- [The book as a PDF](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/p_equals_rp/releases/download/v1.0.0/p_equals_rp.pdf): 337 pages, CC BY 4.0
- [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/p_equals_rp/tree/v1.0.0): the LaTeX source, code and bibliography
- [Report an error or ask a question](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/p_equals_rp/issues): the issues of the book's repository on GitHub
- [Main result: Coding theorem for the queens](https://vsokolov.org/books/p_equals_rp/results.html#coding_theorem_for_the_queens): Theorem 12.1, page 47, proved. NP equals RP exactly when the completions of every queens board can be encoded and decoded in randomized polynomial time at their information content, the logarithm of the completion count up to a logarithmic term.
- [Main result: Product proposals for the queens](https://vsokolov.org/books/p_equals_rp/results.html#product_proposals_for_the_queens): Theorem 30.1, page 116, proved. No importance sampling proposal with independent coordinates can beat crude Monte Carlo for counting N queens by more than a factor given by the entropy deficit of the solution marginals, which is small for N up to 12.
- [Main result: Trapezoid on random nodes for bounded variation, no logarithm](https://vsokolov.org/books/p_equals_rp/results.html#trapezoid_bounded_variation_no_log): Theorem 37.4, page 151, proved. For any integrand of bounded variation V the trapezoid on random ordered nodes has bias at most V over 2(n+1) and mean squared error at most V squared over 2(n+1)(n+2), with no logarithm and no dependence on the number of steps.
- [Main result: Learning the posterior mean matrix is equivalent to NP equals RP](https://vsokolov.org/books/p_equals_rp/results.html#learning_problem_equivalent_to_np_rp): Theorem 42.7, page 181, proved. NP equals RP is equivalent to a randomized polynomial time algorithm, or a uniform polynomial size circuit family, computing the queens posterior mean matrix of every board to relative accuracy one over N squared.
- [Main result: The main equivalence, NP = RP if and only if queens completions can be sampled or counted in polynomial time](https://vsokolov.org/books/p_equals_rp/results.html#main_equivalence_np_rp_queens_sampling): Theorem 58.1, page 242, proved. NP equals RP exactly when the completions of a partial queens placement can be sampled almost uniformly, the level sets of the queens energy can be sampled, or the number of completions can be approximated, in randomized polynomial time.
- [Main result: Conditional FPRAS for the vertical walk with stratified quadrature](https://vsokolov.org/books/p_equals_rp/results.html#conditional_fpras_vertical_walk): Theorem 43.1, page 185, conditional. Given a level set sampler and a ladder of at most 2K rungs with ratios at least one half, the vertical walk with stratified quadrature approximates the ground state count in time K squared over epsilon squared times the sampler cost, so counting reduces to level set sampling.
- [Main result: Expansion of the bottom level set is equivalent to polynomial mixing](https://vsokolov.org/books/p_equals_rp/results.html#expansion_equivalent_to_mixing): Theorem 56.5, page 237, proved. By Cheeger's inequality, a polynomial lower bound on the conductance of the giant component gives polynomial mixing of the lazy swap chain, and polynomial mixing conversely gives the conductance bound.
- [Conditional: ETH and the program (exponential lower bounds for samplers on hard boards)](https://vsokolov.org/books/p_equals_rp/results.html#eth_and_the_program): Theorem 10.3, page 36
- [Open: Existence and form of the rate function of the attack count](https://vsokolov.org/books/p_equals_rp/results.html#attack_rate_function_conjecture): Conjecture 21.1, page 82
- [Open: Mixing of the reflected Laplace walk of log ordinates](https://vsokolov.org/books/p_equals_rp/results.html#reflected_walk_mixing_conjecture): Conjecture 33.1, page 133
- [Open: Vertical likelihood Monte Carlo is polynomial given polynomial level set draws](https://vsokolov.org/books/p_equals_rp/results.html#vertical_likelihood_polynomial_time_conjecture): Conjecture 33.2, page 134
- [Conditional: Conditional FPRAS for the vertical walk with stratified quadrature](https://vsokolov.org/books/p_equals_rp/results.html#conditional_fpras_vertical_walk): Theorem 43.1, page 185
- [Conditional: FPRAS for the unconditioned queens count under mixing hypotheses (sketch)](https://vsokolov.org/books/p_equals_rp/results.html#fpras_unconditioned_queens_count_sketch): Proposition 43.2, page 187
- [Conditional: Conditional FPRAS with an integer ladder from a polynomial level set sampler](https://vsokolov.org/books/p_equals_rp/results.html#conditional_fpras_integer_ladder): Theorem 45.1, page 193, conditional on a polynomial level set sampler for the energy; every ratio of consecutive level sets is at least 1/q for a polynomial q
- [Conditional: A polynomial level set sampler for the queens energy gives NP = RP](https://vsokolov.org/books/p_equals_rp/results.html#queens_energy_sampler_implies_np_rp): Corollary 45.2, page 193
- [Open: Vertical form of the queens conjecture](https://vsokolov.org/books/p_equals_rp/results.html#queens_conjecture_vertical_form): Conjecture 45.7, page 195
- [Open: Mixing of the block chain on unconditioned and reduction boards](https://vsokolov.org/books/p_equals_rp/results.html#block_chain_mixing_conjecture): Conjecture 49.2, page 210
- [Open: Polynomial mixing of the swap chain on the bottom level set of the queens](https://vsokolov.org/books/p_equals_rp/results.html#swap_chain_mixing_conjecture): Conjecture 56.1, page 235
- [Open: Expansion of the bottom level set](https://vsokolov.org/books/p_equals_rp/results.html#expansion_of_the_bottom_level_set): Conjecture 56.4, page 237
- [Conditional: Median form of the hitting set characterisation of prRP = prP](https://vsokolov.org/books/p_equals_rp/results.html#derandomization_equivalence_prrp_prp): Theorem 58.2, page 244
- [Conditional: Rung skipping, the walk that starts at a connected level set](https://vsokolov.org/books/p_equals_rp/results.html#rung_skipping): Theorem 60.20, page 264
- [Open: Shattering depth on hard boards](https://vsokolov.org/books/p_equals_rp/results.html#shattering_depth_conjecture): Conjecture 60.21, page 266
- [Open: Depth growth on random boards](https://vsokolov.org/books/p_equals_rp/results.html#depth_growth_conjecture): Conjecture 60.25, page 269

## Bayes, Artificial Intelligence, and Deep Learning: Foundations of Data Science

To prove, check or extend a result of this book, start with its catalog: each of the 9 results has its exact statement, its status (conditional), its assumptions, its origin, its printed number and page, and the Quarto file of its source. The numbers and pages are those of version 1.0.1 of the PDF. Cite the book and the number of the result.

- [Bayes, Artificial Intelligence, and Deep Learning: Foundations of Data Science](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayes_ai_deep_learning/index.html.md): by Nick Polson and Vadim Sokolov (2026). A textbook that develops Bayesian reasoning, statistical learning and deep learning as one probabilistic framework, from Bayes' rule and decision theory to neural networks, transformers and AI agents, with code in R and Python. Keywords: Bayesian learning, deep learning, statistical learning, large language models, neural networks, probabilistic inference, reinforcement learning, quantile neural networks, AI agents, transformer models, decision theory, Gaussian processes.
- [How to cite](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23603837): DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23603837 for version 1.0.1 (10.5281/zenodo.23603836 for all versions); the BibTeX entry is on the book page
- [Results by chapter](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayes_ai_deep_learning/results.html.md): 9 results with their statements, status and numbers
- [Catalog of results](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/bayes_ai_deep_learning/main/RESULTS.md): 9 results with their statements, status and printed numbers
- [Catalog as data](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/bayes_ai_deep_learning/main/results.yaml): the same results as YAML, each with id, label, name, chapter, origin, status, conditions, summary and statement
- [All facts as JSON](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/bayes_ai_deep_learning/main/site/book.json): title, authors, DOIs, licenses, links, citation, chapters with summaries, and every result with its printed number, page, source file and LaTeX label
- [The book as a PDF](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/bayes_ai_deep_learning/releases/download/v1.0.1/bayes_ai_deep_learning.pdf): 840 pages, CC BY 4.0
- [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/bayes_ai_deep_learning/tree/v1.0.1): the Quarto source, code and bibliography
- [Report an error or ask a question](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/bayes_ai_deep_learning/issues): the issues of the book's repository on GitHub
- [The book as a website](https://vsokolov.org/bayes_ai_deep_learning/): every chapter as a page, with search
- [Main result: Posterior probability that Nakamura did not cheat given a 45 win streak](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayes_ai_deep_learning/results.html#nakamura_streak_posterior_innocence): Example 2.10, page 82, conditional. Under Anand's prior of 1 in 10000 and a binomial model of the streak, the posterior probability that Nakamura did not cheat is 0.9965.
- [Main result: Polya Gamma Gibbs sampler for Bayesian logistic regression](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayes_ai_deep_learning/results.html#polya_gamma_gibbs_sampler_logistic): Section 13.7.1, page 445, conditional. For binomial logistic regression with a Gaussian prior, alternating a Polya Gamma draw of one latent variable per observation with a multivariate normal draw of the coefficients gives a two step Gibbs sampler.
- [Main result: Posterior concentration at the minimax rate for sparse deep learning](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayes_ai_deep_learning/results.html#posterior_concentration_sparse_deep_learning): Section 19.9.2, page 657, conditional. Under smoothness and prior mass conditions, the posterior distribution of the regression function concentrates around the true function at the minimax rate, up to a factor of log N.
- [Main result: Maximum expected utility by a quantile neural network](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayes_ai_deep_learning/results.html#meu_quantile_network_method): Section 21.6.1, page 700, conditional. A network trained with the check loss on simulated utilities, with the decision and the quantile level as inputs, approximates the quantile function of the utility; integrating it over the level approximates the expected utility, and the optimal decision maximizes that integral.
- [Conditional: Posterior probability that Nakamura did not cheat given a 45 win streak](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayes_ai_deep_learning/results.html#nakamura_streak_posterior_innocence): Example 2.10, page 82
- [Conditional: Option value of learning in Bernoulli Beta asset allocation](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayes_ai_deep_learning/results.html#bernoulli_beta_option_value_of_learning): Section 4.2.3, page 162
- [Conditional: Livermore's trading maxims as Bellman value comparisons](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayes_ai_deep_learning/results.html#livermore_maxims_bellman_view): Section 4.2.4, page 163
- [Conditional: Polya Gamma integral identity for binomial likelihoods](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayes_ai_deep_learning/results.html#polya_gamma_integral_identity): Section 13.7.1, page 445
- [Conditional: Polya Gamma Gibbs sampler for Bayesian logistic regression](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayes_ai_deep_learning/results.html#polya_gamma_gibbs_sampler_logistic): Section 13.7.1, page 445
- [Conditional: Bartlett Fejer scale mixture representation of the exponential power prior](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayes_ai_deep_learning/results.html#bayesian_bridge_bartlett_fejer_mixture): Section 17.11.1, page 602
- [Conditional: Posterior concentration at the minimax rate for sparse deep learning](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayes_ai_deep_learning/results.html#posterior_concentration_sparse_deep_learning): Section 19.9.2, page 657
- [Conditional: Maximum expected utility by a quantile neural network](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayes_ai_deep_learning/results.html#meu_quantile_network_method): Section 21.6.1, page 700

## Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times

To prove, check or extend a result of this book, start with its catalog: each of the 472 results has its exact statement, its status (proved, computed, conditional, open or counterexample), its assumptions, its origin, its printed number and page, and the LaTeX file of its source. The numbers and pages are those of version 1.4.0 of the PDF. Cite the book and the number of the result.

- [Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/index.html.md): by Nicholas G. Polson and Vadim Sokolov (2026). Computes the Thorin measure whose positivity is equivalent to the Riemann Hypothesis, from Pólya's integral for Xi in certified ball arithmetic, and proves that finite positivity tests on the heat trace cannot decide it; with hitting times, friable approximants, the reciprocal zeta function and Lee Yang theory. Keywords: Riemann hypothesis, zeros of the zeta function, Thorin measures, generalized gamma convolutions, Pólya densities, Brownian hitting times, reciprocal zeta function, de Bruijn Newman constant, Keiper Li coefficients, infinitely divisible distributions, Lee Yang theorem, certified ball arithmetic.
- [How to cite](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23595861): DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23595861 for version 1.4.0 (10.5281/zenodo.23331089 for all versions); the BibTeX entry is on the book page
- [Results by chapter](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html.md): 472 results with their statements, status and numbers
- [Catalog of results](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/main/RESULTS.md): 472 results with their statements, status and printed numbers
- [Catalog as data](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/main/results.yaml): the same results as YAML, each with id, label, name, chapter, origin, status, conditions, summary and statement
- [All facts as JSON](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/main/site/book.json): title, authors, DOIs, licenses, links, citation, chapters with summaries, and every result with its printed number, page, source file and LaTeX label
- [The book as a PDF](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/releases/download/v1.4.0/computing_rh.pdf): 934 pages, CC BY 4.0
- [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/tree/v1.4.0): the LaTeX source, code and bibliography
- [Report an error or ask a question](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/issues): the issues of the book's repository on GitHub
- [Main result: Bosch type theorem for the reciprocal Xi function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#reciprocal_xi_power_hcm_threshold): Theorem 4.3.5, page 75, proved. The reciprocal Xi function composed with the power x to the p is HCM exactly when the absolute value of p is at most one minus twice the largest zero angle over pi, so RH is the extreme case p equal to one.
- [Main result: Derivative signs of the heat trace up to order 1.16 x 10^25](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#heat_trace_derivative_signs_to_order_1e25): Theorem 5.1.13, page 112, proved. From the verification of RH to height 3 times 10^12, every derivative of the heat trace alternates in sign, equivalently the Williamson measures are positive, up to order 1.16 times 10^25, with the numerical inequalities of the proof certified in ball arithmetic.
- [Main result: Biane form lower bound for the collision time of zeros under the backward heat flow](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#backward_heat_flow_biane_form_collision_bound): Theorem 8.4.8, page 239, proved. While all zeros of a real polynomial stay real and simple, a gap between two adjacent zeros cannot close under the backward heat flow before the time one over the minimum of Laguerre's quantity over the gap, a bound at least as strong as the one from the critical point and attained by z squared minus a squared.
- [Main result: Clock of Pólya's Bessel function as a hitting time of an explicit diffusion](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#clock_of_polya_bessel_function_hitting_time_of_explicit_diffusion): Theorem 8.7.10, page 313, proved. The index side clock of Pólya's Bessel function, the GGC with Thorin atoms at the squares of the positive zeros of nu maps to K_{i nu}(2 pi), is the clock of a hitting time of a level by an explicit diffusion, planar Brownian motion killed at rate one half and Doob transformed by K_0.
- [Main result: Minimum of the Thorin density at the origin and stable summand at the basepoint one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_density_minimum_at_origin_basepoint_one): Proposition 9.1.11, page 340, proved. With no hypothesis on the zeros, certified with the first 1800 zeros in ball arithmetic and explicit zero counts above height 2000, the Thorin density of the shifted clock at the basepoint one is smallest only at the origin, so the clock is the sum of an independent positive stable one half variable and a generalized gamma convolution.
- [Main result: Almost GGC theorem for the shifted clocks](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#almost_ggc_theorem): Theorem 11.4.2, page 462, proved. With no hypothesis, for every basepoint between one half and one the Cauchy kernels of the zeros to the right of the basepoint carry a vanishing fraction of the mass of the kernels of the other zeros, with a power saving from zero density estimates.
- [Main result: Total variation distance from the Pólya law to ferromagnetic laws is below two millionths, with no hypothesis](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#polya_law_within_total_variation_two_millionths_of_a_ferromagnetic_law): Proposition 13.4.6, page 538, proved. With no hypothesis the total variation distance from the Pólya law to the ferromagnetic laws is below 1.932 × 10^-6 by a certified computation in ball arithmetic and below 1.266 × 10^-4 by an explicit construction, and it is zero exactly when the Riemann Hypothesis holds.
- [Main result: Threshold theorem along the flow for the shifted clocks of the heat flow function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#threshold_theorem_shifted_clock_along_heat_flow): Theorem 15.2.3, page 583, proved. For every time $t\ge0$ and basepoint $\alpha\ge\frac12$, the shifted clock of the heat flow function $\xi_t$ is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution exactly when no zero of $\xi_t$ has real part above $\alpha$, and its Thorin measure is then an explicit sum of Cauchy kernels and atoms over the zeros.
- [Main result: Phase diagram theorem, de Bruijn's strip theorem in Thorin form](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#phase_diagram_theorem_de_bruijn_strip_theorem_in_thorin_form): Theorem 15.3.2, page 584, proved. The set of points $(t,\alpha)$ where the shifted clock of the heat flow function is a generalized gamma convolution is carried along parabolas by the flow (de Bruijn's strip theorem in Thorin form), the de Bruijn Newman constant is the minimum of $t+2(\alpha-\frac12)^2$ over it, and RH holds exactly when the corner $(0,\frac12)$ belongs to it.
- [Main result: Unconditional GGC property of the reciprocal Xi function in the fourth root variable, compensated by the first power sum, with explicit Thorin density from the heat trace](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#heat_trace_weighted_reciprocal_xi_in_fourth_root_is_ggc_with_absolutely_continuous_thorin_measure): Proposition 9.1.7, page 336, proved. Unconditionally, the function $\Psi(s)=\frac{\xi(\frac12+s^{1/4})}{\xi(\frac12)}e^{-p_1\sqrt s}$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution whose Thorin measure has an explicit density built from the heat trace $W$, and under RH it equals the Weierstrass product $\prod_{\gamma>0}(1+\sqrt s/\gamma^2)e^{-\sqrt s/\gamma^2}$.
- [Main result: RH is equivalent to boundedness of the heat trace of the zeros on a vertical line](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rh_equivalent_to_boundedness_of_heat_trace_on_vertical_line): Theorem 5.1.4, page 98, proved. The Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if the heat trace $v\mapsto W(\sigma+iv)$ of the zeros is bounded on the real line, for one, equivalently every, $\sigma>0$.
- [Main result: Concentration of the Laguerre expressions at the origin along the whole de Bruijn Newman flow, with positivity of $L_{n,t}$ on every window for large $n$ (Newton 2026, Zenodo)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#laguerre_expression_central_second_moment_vanishes_uniformly_along_de_bruijn_newman_flow): Theorem 8.4.20, page 252, proved. For the probability measures $\mathbb{E}_{n,t}$ defining the Laguerre expressions $L_{n,t}$ of the de Bruijn Newman function, the second moment of the centred variable tends to zero uniformly in $0\le t\le\frac12$, so for every $X$ the expression $L_{n,t}(x)$ is positive on $|x|\le X$ for all large $n$, uniformly in $t$ (Newton 2026, Zenodo); the index is not effective.
- [Main result: RH holds if and only if the density of the clock is a Pólya frequency function of infinite order](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rh_equivalent_to_clock_density_being_polya_frequency_function_of_infinite_order): Proposition 8.1.2, page 211, proved. RH is equivalent to the density $f$ of the clock being a Pólya frequency function of infinite order, the one sided form of the two sided criterion: under RH $f$ is the density of $\sum_\gamma e_\gamma/\gamma^2$, and conversely Schoenberg's theorem forces $G$ to have only real zeros.
- [Main result: RH holds if and only if a freely infinitely divisible law nu_xi with free cumulant transform log xi(1/2)/xi(1/2+sqrt(-z)) exists](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rh_equivalent_to_existence_of_freely_infinitely_divisible_law_with_cumulant_transform_log_xi_ratio): Proposition 11.2.4, page 442, proved. RH holds exactly when the function $\mathcal{C}_\xi(z)=\log\{\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt{-z})\}$ is the free cumulant transform of a freely infinitely divisible probability measure, which under RH is $\Lambda_{\rm BP}(\mu_0)$, with compact support, free cumulants $m_{n-1}/n$ and free Lévy measure $N(y^{-1/2})dy/y$.
- [Main result: No reweighting of Riemann's theta series by summable weights has infinitely many real zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#no_summable_reweighting_of_the_theta_series_has_infinitely_many_real_zeros): Theorem 22.2.4, page 764, proved. For nonzero real weights $w_n$ with $\sum|w_n|n^{-\sigma}<\infty$ for every $\sigma>0$ (this includes the friable truncations), the reweighted function has finitely many real zeros and infinitely many nonreal zeros.
- [Main result: Paired form: zeta has no zero to the right of alpha exactly when the real and imaginary parts of xi on the line alpha interlace](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#paired_form_of_the_cosh_ladder_hermite_biehler_equivalence_with_zero_free_half_plane): Theorem 22.13.3, page 785, proved. For $\alpha>\frac12$, zeta has no zero with real part at least $\alpha$ exactly when $E_\alpha(z)=\xi(\alpha-iz)$ is Hermite Biehler, exactly when the real and imaginary parts of $\xi(\alpha+it)$ have only real simple strictly interlacing zeros; hence RH holds if and only if this holds for every $\alpha>\frac12$.
- [Main result: No HCM: sums of exponentials are not HCM, and the continued reciprocal xi density has a computed zero in the right half plane](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#no_hcm_density_for_sums_of_exponentials_and_a_computed_zero_of_the_continued_density): Theorem 24.5.7, page 817, conditional on for part (ii), an explicit remainder bound for the omitted terms on a sector containing $z_*$. No density of a sum of $n\ge2$ independent exponentials with distinct rates is HCM (proved); the continuation of $f$ from its first 120 residue terms vanishes at $z_*=0.01383187+0.02000180i$ (computed), which proves $f$ is not HCM once the omitted terms are controlled on a sector containing $z_*$.
- [Main result: The Euler hitting times converge after scaling to a spectrally positive stable law of index 3/2](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#universal_three_halves_stable_limit_of_the_euler_hitting_times): Theorem 24.8.2, page 828, proved. As $P\to\infty$, $Z_P=(Y_P-\kappa_2(P))/\kappa_3(P)^{2/3}\Rightarrow Z$ with $\log\mathbb Ee^{-sZ}=(2s)^{3/2}/6$, with the bound $|\log\mathbb Ee^{-sZ_P}-(2s)^{3/2}/6|\le\frac{|s|^2}6\rho_4(P)$ for $\operatorname{Re}s\ge0$ and $\rho_4(P)\to0$.
- [Main result: Thorin rigidity: any factorisation of the reciprocal xi law into two GGC laws forces RH and splits the zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_rigidity_of_ggc_factorisations_of_the_reciprocal_xi_law): Theorem 24.9.1, page 830, proved. If $\mu=\mu_1*\mu_2$ with both factors GGC, then RH holds and the Thorin measures are $\sum a_\gamma\delta_{\gamma^2}$ and $\sum(m_\gamma-a_\gamma)\delta_{\gamma^2}$ with $0\le a_\gamma\le m_\gamma$; no GGC law with drift or a nonzero absolutely continuous Thorin part is a GGC factor with a GGC cofactor.
- [Main result: Prime built GGC hitting times converge to the base point laws for theta < beta < 2 - theta under QRH(theta)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#prime_built_ggc_hitting_times_converge_to_the_base_point_laws_under_qrh_theta): Theorem 24.15.4, page 847, conditional on the quasi Riemann hypothesis QRH($\theta$) for some $\theta<1$ (every nontrivial zero has real part at most $\theta$). Assume QRH($\theta$) and $\theta<\beta<2-\theta$. Then $|d_X(t)-\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}\xi'/\xi(\beta+it)|\ll_\beta X^{\theta-\beta}\log(t+2)$ uniformly in $t$, $d_X\ge0$ for $X\ge X_0(\beta,\theta)$, the GGC laws $\mu^{(\beta)}_X$ with Thorin density $d_X$ converge weakly to $\mu^{(\beta)}$, and conversely nonnegativity of $d_X(t)$ for large $X$ at one $\beta$ gives QRH($\beta$).
- [Open: Positivity of the Thorin density on one line, open question](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#one_line_positivity_exclusion_open): Remark 1.2.4, page 15
- [Open: Question: for which beta is the density of W^beta HCM](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_hcm_powers_of_mellin_variable_w): Question 4.2.7, page 72
- [Open: Question: does HCM of W^beta for a single beta imply RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_single_power_hcm_implies_rh): Question 4.2.8, page 72
- [Open: Question: HCM exponent of the deformed reciprocal Xi function for negative time](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_hcm_exponent_deficit_negative_heat_time): Question 4.3.11, page 79
- [Conditional: Thorin measure of X_p under RH: scaled Lamperti laws (Bosch's variable)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_measure_of_reciprocal_xi_power_under_rh_lamperti_kernel): Corollary 4.3.13, page 80, conditional on the Riemann Hypothesis
- [Open: Question: construct X_{1/2} from Brownian motion without the zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_construct_x_half_without_zeros): Question 4.3.15, page 81
- [Open: Question: prove positivity of u_p for all p without locating zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_thorin_density_positive_for_all_powers): Question 4.3.16, page 81
- [Open: Question: natural boundary of the clock density](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_natural_boundary_of_clock_density): Question 4.3.21, page 83
- [Conditional: Natural boundary of the clock density under RH, simple zeros and gap hypotheses](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#clock_density_natural_boundary_under_gap_hypotheses): Theorem 4.3.22, page 84
- [Open: Question: for which p are X_p and its Cauchy analogue HCM](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_which_powers_of_clock_variable_are_hcm): Question 4.3.24, page 85
- [Conditional: First gap theorem: HCM of W^beta forces |beta| at least gamma_2 minus gamma_1](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#first_gap_necessary_condition_for_hcm_of_w_power): Theorem 4.3.27, page 88
- [Open: Question: first gap conjecture for HCM powers of W](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_first_gap_conjecture): Question 4.3.28, page 88
- [Open: Refined first gap conjecture for sums of Laplace variables](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_first_gap_conjecture_refined): Question 4.3.29, page 90
- [Conditional: There is no Gaussian smoothing criterion for RH on a line with real part alpha above one half](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#no_gaussian_criterion_on_vertical_line_alpha_above_one_half_under_rh): Proposition 5.1.12, page 110, conditional on The Riemann Hypothesis: every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part $\frac12$
- [Conditional: Thorin type measure of the normalised reciprocal zeta function under RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_measure_normalised_reciprocal_zeta_under_rh): Theorem 6.1.10, page 142, conditional on The Riemann Hypothesis: every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part $\frac12$
- [Conditional: Sawtooth expansion of the argument function after Gaussian averaging, under RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#sawtooth_expansion_argument_function_gaussian_average): Corollary 6.1.14, page 145, conditional on The Riemann Hypothesis: every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part $\frac12$
- [Counterexample: A harmonic mean of two GGC transforms that is not a Laplace transform of a positive measure](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#harmonic_mean_of_two_ggc_transforms_not_a_laplace_transform): Example 7.1.24, page 188

## Clinical Trials in Practice: From Foundations to AI Agents

- [Clinical Trials in Practice: From Foundations to AI Agents](https://vsokolov.org/books/clinical_trials_in_practice/index.html.md): by Alexandra Sokolova and Vadim Sokolov (2026). Clinical trials as science and as regulated operations: design and statistics, the daily work of a Phase III study from site selection to the trial master file, regulatory submission, and what AI agents may and may not do in regulated research. Keywords: clinical trials, Phase III trials, clinical trial operations, adaptive trial design, Bayesian clinical trials, Good Clinical Practice, regulatory submission, trial master file, clinical data management, drug development, real world evidence, AI agents in clinical research.

## On Statistical Methods for Genetics: Fisher, Ewens and the Bayesian Programme

To prove, check or extend a result of this book, start with its catalog: each of the 58 results has its exact statement, its status (proved or open), its assumptions, its origin, its printed number and page, and the LaTeX file of its source. The numbers and pages are those of version 1.0.1 of the PDF. Cite the book and the number of the result.

- [On Statistical Methods for Genetics: Fisher, Ewens and the Bayesian Programme](https://vsokolov.org/books/statistical_methods_genetics/index.html.md): by Nicholas G. Polson (2026). Statistical theory of population genetics: an exact form of Fisher's Fundamental Theorem, shrinkage estimates of the rate of adaptation, the Ewens sampling formula and its rigidity, rational conjugacy, and sufficiency for learned coalescent inference. Keywords: population genetics, Fundamental Theorem of Natural Selection, Ewens sampling formula, Pitman Yor process, Poisson Dirichlet distribution, horseshoe prior, Pochhammer priors, Kingman coalescent, approximate Bayesian computation, sufficiency without a likelihood.
- [How to cite](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23509850): DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23509850 for version 1.0.1 (10.5281/zenodo.23509612 for all versions); the BibTeX entry is on the book page
- [Results by chapter](https://vsokolov.org/books/statistical_methods_genetics/results.html.md): 58 results with their statements, status and numbers
- [Catalog of results](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/statistical_methods_genetics/main/RESULTS.md): 58 results with their statements, status and printed numbers
- [Catalog as data](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/statistical_methods_genetics/main/results.yaml): the same results as YAML, each with id, label, name, chapter, origin, status, conditions, summary and statement
- [All facts as JSON](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/statistical_methods_genetics/main/site/book.json): title, authors, DOIs, licenses, links, citation, chapters with summaries, and every result with its printed number, page, source file and LaTeX label
- [The book as a PDF](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/statistical_methods_genetics/releases/download/v1.0.1/statistical_methods_genetics.pdf): 489 pages, CC BY 4.0
- [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/statistical_methods_genetics/tree/v1.0.1): the LaTeX source, code and bibliography
- [Report an error or ask a question](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/statistical_methods_genetics/issues): the issues of the book's repository on GitHub
- [Main result: Whole genome Fundamental Theorem decomposition](https://vsokolov.org/books/statistical_methods_genetics/results.html#whole_genome): Theorem 3.5, page 66, proved. For arbitrary genotype frequency paths, the rate of change of mean Malthusian fitness splits exactly into an additive part and a remainder; the remainder vanishes whenever the log frequencies move inside the span of the gene contents, and it vanishes for every assignment of fitnesses only then.
- [Main result: Exact remainder for one locus with k alleles](https://vsokolov.org/books/statistical_methods_genetics/results.html#exact_remainder_one_locus_alleles): Theorem 3.16, page 76, proved. In the one locus random mating model with constant fitnesses, the change in mean fitness is the additive term divided by mean fitness plus an explicit quadratic remainder in the dominance deviations.
- [Main result: Oracle shrinkage understates the additive variance](https://vsokolov.org/books/statistical_methods_genetics/results.html#oracle_shrinkage_understates_the_additive_variance): Proposition 4.10, page 140, proved. Shrinkage tuned to estimate each average effect as well as possible necessarily understates the additive variance, by an explicit amount.
- [Main result: Shrinkage weights are stick breaking weights](https://vsokolov.org/books/statistical_methods_genetics/results.html#shrinkage_weights_are_stick_breaking_weights): Theorem 5.15, page 180, proved. The Beta law of the horseshoe type shrinkage weight is exactly the law of the first stick breaking weight of the two parameter GEM family, which links shrinkage priors to Ewens Pitman partitions.
- [Main result: Rigidity of the residual allocation structure](https://vsokolov.org/books/statistical_methods_genetics/results.html#py_thm_rigid): Theorem 7.11, page 271, proved. Among sampling densities that charge every interval, only power weights keep the induced subdivision of the size biased layout a residual allocation model, so for a discount strictly between zero and one no such density other than the uniform one carries a two parameter Poisson Dirichlet law to the stick breaking sequence of another member of the family.
- [Main result: A bottleneck that attains the Bayes risk is sufficient](https://vsokolov.org/books/statistical_methods_genetics/results.html#a_bottleneck_that_attains_the_bayes_risk_is_sufficient): Theorem 10.12, page 399, proved. If a learned map that factors through a summary of the data attains the minimal check loss, the summary is sufficient, so sufficiency can be tested by comparing risks.
- [Main result: The number of segregating sites is not sufficient for theta, likelihood argument](https://vsokolov.org/books/statistical_methods_genetics/results.html#is_not_sufficient_for): Proposition 11.12, page 443, proved. The conditional law of the infinite sites data given the site count depends on theta through the latent tree, shown explicitly for three and four sequences.
- [Main result: DeepSets encoders factor through the site frequency spectrum](https://vsokolov.org/books/statistical_methods_genetics/results.html#deepsets_encoders_factor_through_the_spectrum): Theorem 11.16, page 445, proved. Any encoder built from per site permutation invariant features depends on the data only through the site frequency spectrum, which caps what such an encoder can learn.
- [Open: Conjecture, rigidity of Poisson Dirichlet under general ascertainment](https://vsokolov.org/books/statistical_methods_genetics/results.html#future_conj_rigid): Conjecture 12.7, page 467
- [Chapter 1. A Short History of Population Genetics](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/statistical_methods_genetics/main/summaries/01_a_short_history_of_population_genetics.md): summary of the chapter and its results
- [Chapter 2. A Mathematical Toolkit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/statistical_methods_genetics/main/summaries/02_a_mathematical_toolkit.md): summary of the chapter and its results
- [Chapter 3. The Fundamental Theorem of Natural Selection: From Deterministic to Stochastic, Fisher to Bayes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/statistical_methods_genetics/main/summaries/03_the_fundamental_theorem_of_natural_selection.md): summary of the chapter and its results

Pólya Inverse Gamma Posteriors, Fisher's Species Model, and Good's Predictive Rule for the Ewens Sampling Problem](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/statistical_methods_genetics/main/summaries/08_polya_inverse_gamma_posteriors_fishers_species_model.md): summary of the chapter and its results

## On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods

To prove, check or extend a result of this book, start with its catalog: each of the 194 results has its exact statement, its status (proved, conditional or open), its assumptions, its origin, its printed number and page, and the LaTeX file of its source. The numbers and pages are those of version 1.2.0 of the PDF. Cite the book and the number of the result.

- [On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/index.html.md): by Nick Polson and Vadim Sokolov (2026). What probability can and cannot contribute to the Langlands programme: Sato Tate laws, random walks on trees and isogeny graphs, Thorin measures and generalized gamma convolutions as reformulations of the Riemann hypothesis, and Bayesian identification of Sato Tate groups, with code and data. Keywords: Langlands programme, Sato Tate law, Frobenius traces, automorphic L functions, generalized Riemann hypothesis, Thorin measures, generalized gamma convolutions, random walks on trees, supersingular isogeny graphs, random matrix theory, Poisson Dirichlet law, critical percolation, Bayesian inference.
- [How to cite](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23503453): DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23503453 for version 1.2.0 (10.5281/zenodo.23419247 for all versions); the BibTeX entry is on the book page
- [Results by chapter](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html.md): 194 results with their statements, status and numbers
- [Catalog of results](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/langlands/main/RESULTS.md): 194 results with their statements, status and printed numbers
- [Catalog as data](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/langlands/main/results.yaml): the same results as YAML, each with id, label, name, chapter, origin, status, conditions, summary and statement
- [All facts as JSON](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/langlands/main/site/book.json): title, authors, DOIs, licenses, links, citation, chapters with summaries, and every result with its printed number, page, source file and LaTeX label
- [The book as a PDF](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/langlands/releases/download/v1.2.0/langlands.pdf): 700 pages, CC BY 4.0
- [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/langlands/tree/v1.2.0): the LaTeX source, code and bibliography
- [Report an error or ask a question](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/langlands/issues): the issues of the book's repository on GitHub
- [Main result: Equidistribution does not determine automorphy](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#equidistribution_does_not_determine_automorphy): Proposition 1.5, page 7, proved. Sato Tate equidistribution of a sequence indexed by the primes cannot certify that it comes from a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL(2) with trivial central character, because altering such a sequence on an infinite set of primes of density zero leaves the limiting empirical averages of all continuous functions unchanged but, by Ramakrishnan's refinement of strong multiplicity one, makes it nonautomorphic, and continuum many equidistributed sequences are not automorphic.
- [Main result: Limit of the normalised Kemeny constants of supersingular isogeny graphs](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#kemeny_constant_supersingular_isogeny_graphs_limit): Theorem 10.6, page 151, proved. As the characteristic grows through primes congruent to 1 modulo 12, with the prime isogeny degree fixed, the mean time for simple random walk on a supersingular isogeny graph to hit a uniformly random curve is asymptotic to the number of vertices times the expected number of visits of simple random walk on the regular tree of the same degree to its starting point, so about twice the number of vertices for 2 isogenies.
- [Main result: Thorin criteria for the generalized Riemann hypothesis of automorphic L functions](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#thorin_criteria_generalized_riemann_hypothesis_automorphic): Theorem 14.8, page 220, proved. The generalized Riemann hypothesis for the L function of a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL(n) over the rationals, and the Riemann hypothesis for zeta, are each equivalent to several positivity statements, among them that the reciprocal of the self dual completion, read in the squared variable, is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution whose Thorin measure sits at the squared ordinates of the zeros, and a Hankel criterion computable from central derivatives; the theorem is an equivalence that extends the first author's 2018 paper, and it proves no case of either hypothesis.
- [Main result: Thorin criterion for the Ramanujan Petersson conjecture at a prime](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#ramanujan_petersson_local_thorin_criterion): Corollary 15.4, page 238, proved. For a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL(2) over the rationals with trivial central character, the Ramanujan Petersson conjecture at an unramified prime (outside the degenerate case of trace 2) holds exactly when the reciprocal of the symmetrised Euler factor, read in the squared variable, is the Laplace transform of a probability law, which is then a generalized gamma convolution whose Thorin measure is a periodic comb (Ramanujan is local Thorin, as the generalized Riemann hypothesis is global Thorin); the corollary is an equivalence and proves no case of the conjecture.
- [Main result: Thorin structure of passage times of the Hecke walk on the regular tree](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#thorin_structure_hecke_walk_passage_times_tree): Theorem 15.15, page 246, proved. The first time that continuous time simple random walk on a regular tree (the Hecke walk, on the Bruhat Tits tree when the degree is a prime plus one) reaches distance n from its start is a generalized gamma convolution whose Thorin atoms, given by the zeros of the sphere polynomials of the tree, lie in the Kesten band and follow the arcsine law as n grows, with an exact mean, a variance linear in n and a central limit theorem; Thorin support in the Kesten band is the random walk form of the Ramanujan bound, and this unconditional theorem about the tree proves no case of the Ramanujan conjecture for automorphic forms.
- [Main result: Gamma process limit of the Frobenius labelled factorisation of a random integer](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#frobenius_labelled_factorisation_gamma_process_limit): Theorem 20.18, page 350, proved. As the parameter of a zeta distributed random integer decreases to one, the logarithms of its prime power factors, multiplied by the parameter minus one and labelled by any equidistributed sequence of points such as Frobenius classes or Sato Tate angles, converge in law to the jumps of a standard Gamma subordinator carrying independent labels drawn from the equidistribution law, and the labelled logarithm converges in law to a Gamma random measure, so that equidistribution becomes a Gamma process.
- [Main result: Extreme value representation of L functions of eta products](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#extreme_value_representation_of_eta_product_l_functions): Theorem 29.7, page 541, proved. For every eta product, that is every product of the functions eta(m tau) raised to nonnegative integer powers r_m with the sum of m r_m equal to 24 (the thirty multiplicative eta products among them), the L function is entire and equals at every complex point the expectation of a regularised incomplete gamma function evaluated at an explicit maximum of exponential clocks, so its values at positive real points are probabilities strictly between zero and one that increase strictly to one.
- [Main result: Consistency of Bayes factors under equidistribution](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#consistency_of_bayes_factors_under_equidistribution): Theorem 31.1, page 571, proved. For any deterministic sequence, such as normalised Frobenius traces, that is equidistributed for a true law with finitely many atoms and finite Kullback Leibler divergence from one candidate law, and with a log likelihood ratio continuous off the atoms, the clipped log Bayes factor between two candidate laws is asymptotically linear in the number of observations, and as the clipping level grows its slope tends to the difference of the divergences of the true law from the two candidates, with no independence assumed.
- [Open: Sato Tate discrepancy vanishes at the square root scale in logarithmic density](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#sato_tate_discrepancy_logarithmic_density_conjecture): Conjecture 5.3, page 68
- [Open: Variance at finite height of the log modulus of the L function of Delta](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#finite_height_variance_conjecture_for_delta): Conjecture 12.6, page 179

## On the Collatz Conjecture: Martingales, Momentum and Continued Fractions

To prove, check or extend a result of this book, start with its catalog: each of the 66 results has its exact statement, its status (proved, conditional or open), its assumptions, its origin, its printed number and page, and the LaTeX file of its source. The numbers and pages are those of version 1.1.0 of the PDF. Cite the book and the number of the result.

- [On the Collatz Conjecture: Martingales, Momentum and Continued Fractions](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/index.html.md): by Nick Polson and Vadim Sokolov (2026). Why the Collatz (3x+1) conjecture resists proof: the map as a random walk, an optimizer and a Diophantine problem; proofs that fixed horizon monotone Lyapunov certificates and finite residue sieves cannot settle it and the cycle inequality cannot exclude all cycles; a momentum method from log2 3. Keywords: Collatz conjecture, 3x+1 problem, Syracuse map, parity vectors, Lyapunov functions, majorization minimization, Nesterov momentum, martingales, continued fractions, Collatz cycles, Diophantine approximation, first order optimization methods.
- [How to cite](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23421852): DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23421852 for version 1.1.0 (10.5281/zenodo.23331099 for all versions); the BibTeX entry is on the book page
- [Results by chapter](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html.md): 66 results with their statements, status and numbers
- [Catalog of results](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/collatz/main/RESULTS.md): 66 results with their statements, status and printed numbers
- [Catalog as data](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/collatz/main/results.yaml): the same results as YAML, each with id, label, name, chapter, origin, status, conditions, summary and statement
- [All facts as JSON](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/collatz/main/site/book.json): title, authors, DOIs, licenses, links, citation, chapters with summaries, and every result with its printed number, page, source file and LaTeX label
- [The book as a PDF](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/collatz/releases/download/v1.1.0/collatz.pdf): 379 pages, CC BY 4.0
- [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/collatz/tree/v1.1.0): the LaTeX source, code and bibliography
- [Report an error or ask a question](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/collatz/issues): the issues of the book's repository on GitHub
- [Main result: No fixed horizon monotone certificate for Collatz descent](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#no_fixed_horizon_monotone_certificate): Corollary 4.15, page 78, proved. For every fixed number J of strides, no strictly increasing function of x certifies descent over J Syracuse strides, because the odd integers congruent to minus 1 modulo 2 to the J+1 ascend for J strides in a row.
- [Main result: Noise bound for Switching MM uniform in the normalized step](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#smm_variance_bound_uniform_in_normalized_step): Proposition 8.7, page 130, proved. On a quadratic with additive gradient noise, on every eigendirection with normalized step up to one, the stationary variance of Switching MM lies between that of gradient descent and 5/3 times it, uniformly over momentum coefficients below one, whereas every step momentum amplifies slow mode noise by a factor that grows without bound as the coefficient tends to one.
- [Main result: Gain weight theorem for the noise floor of periodic first order methods](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#gain_weight_theorem): Theorem 8.12, page 135, proved. For any linear periodic first order method on a quadratic that is stable at zero normalized step and has positive total gain, the slow mode noise floor at matched speed relative to gradient descent is a Cauchy and Schwarz ratio of the step gains, at least one, and equal to one only when all gains are equal.
- [Main result: Exact linear rate of Switching MM on smooth strongly convex functions](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#smm_linear_rate_on_smooth_strongly_convex_functions): Theorem 9.9, page 164, proved. For strongly convex and L smooth functions, two steps of Switching MM at step one over L contract the distance to the minimizer by the product of the classical one step factors of a long and a short gradient step, which explicit functions show is the exact worst case over the class, and the function gap by its square, using the one step function value bound of Taylor, Hendrickx and Glineur (2018).
- [Main result: Diophantine insufficiency, infinitely many cycle lengths survive any verification range](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#diophantine_insufficiency_cycle_lengths): Proposition 11.20, page 205, proved. However far the verification of the Collatz conjecture is pushed, infinitely many cycle lengths survive the cycle inequality, so information about the approximation of log2 3 alone cannot exclude all nontrivial cycles, a point Halbeisen and Hungerbühler (1997) made earlier in another form.
- [Main result: Residue certificates cannot prove descent for all integers (the exceptional 2 adic set)](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#residue_certificates_cannot_prove_descent_for_all_integers): Proposition 15.1, page 267, proved. No residue certificate of finite level can certify descent for every integer, because every residue class it leaves uncovered contains infinitely many positive integers, while the 2 adic integers with infinite coefficient stopping time form a closed null set that contains a point of each known negative cycle.
- [Open: Transient bound conjecture for the injection matrix of Switching MM](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#smm_transient_bound_conjecture): Conjecture 9.7, page 163
- [Conditional: Every switching rule between descent and injection is stable on quadratics, conditional on the transient bound](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#every_switching_rule_is_stable_on_quadratics): Corollary 9.8, page 163
- [Open: Exact convex worst case of Switching MM (conjecture)](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#switching_mm_exact_worst_case_conjecture): Conjecture 10.6, page 174
- [Conditional: What arithmetic would suffice to exclude all Collatz cycles](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#what_arithmetic_would_suffice): Corollary 11.22, page 207
- [Open: Cesàro liminf conjecture on the running mean of the halving exponents](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#cesaro_liminf_conjecture): Conjecture 12.6, page 224
- [Conditional: A bounded form of Tao's theorem would imply the Collatz conjecture, given the positive density theorems](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#bounded_tao_would_imply_collatz_given_positive_density): Proposition 13.3, page 241
- [Open: Conjectured exact worst case rate of Switching MM on smooth convex functions, both branches](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#switching_mm_exact_convex_rate_conjecture): Conjecture 17.2, page 292
- [Open: Trajectory mixing of Syracuse residues modulo powers of 3](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#trajectory_mixing_of_syracuse_residues): Problem O2, page 315
- [Open: Failure fraction of Lyapunov potentials of growing depth for the Syracuse map](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#failure_fraction_of_potentials_of_growing_depth): Problem O3$'$, page 316

- [Open: Arithmetic sharpening of the window bound on the least element of a Collatz cycle](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#arithmetic_sharpening_of_the_cycle_window): Problem C1, page 317

- [Open: Bounded form of Tao's theorem: orbit minimum at most 2^71 on a set of logarithmic density one](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#bounded_form_of_tao_theorem): Problem B1, page 318
- [Open: True decay rate of the Fourier coefficients of the Syracuse random variable modulo powers of 3](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#true_decay_rate_of_syracuse_fourier_coefficients): Problem B2, page 318
- [Open: Sharpness of Shaik's threshold 3/log(4/3) for total stopping times](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#sharpness_of_shaik_threshold_for_stopping_times): Problem B3, page 319
- [Open: Exact worst case function gap rate of Switching MM for small condition numbers](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#exact_function_gap_rate_of_switching_mm_for_small_condition_numbers): Problem S1, page 319

## On Hilbert's 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation

To prove, check or extend a result of this book, start with its catalog: each of the 92 results has its exact statement, its status (proved, conditional, open or counterexample), its assumptions, its origin, its printed number and page, and the LaTeX file of its source. The numbers and pages are those of version 1.0.1 of the PDF. Cite the book and the number of the result.

- [On Hilbert's 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/index.html.md): by Nick Polson and Vadim Sokolov (2026). Hilbert's sixth problem from Kolmogorov's axioms and the Boltzmann equation to the Navier Stokes equations, and the inverse passage: Bayesian estimation on the solution manifold of a differential equation, where the adjoint evolution of the data is a sufficient statistic for linear equations. Keywords: Hilbert's sixth problem, foundations of probability, kinetic theory, Boltzmann equation, Navier Stokes equations, hydrodynamic limits, Bayesian inverse problems, sufficient statistics, generative Bayesian computation, large deviations, stochastic mechanics, statistical mechanics.
- [How to cite](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23407620): DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23407620 for version 1.0.1 (10.5281/zenodo.23327514 for all versions); the BibTeX entry is on the book page
- [Results by chapter](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/results.html.md): 92 results with their statements, status and numbers
- [Catalog of results](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/hilbert6/main/RESULTS.md): 92 results with their statements, status and printed numbers
- [Catalog as data](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/hilbert6/main/results.yaml): the same results as YAML, each with id, label, name, chapter, origin, status, conditions, summary and statement
- [All facts as JSON](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/hilbert6/main/site/book.json): title, authors, DOIs, licenses, links, citation, chapters with summaries, and every result with its printed number, page, source file and LaTeX label
- [The book as a PDF](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/hilbert6/releases/download/v1.0.1/hilbert6.pdf): 548 pages, CC BY 4.0
- [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/hilbert6/tree/v1.0.1): the LaTeX source, code and bibliography
- [Report an error or ask a question](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/hilbert6/issues): the issues of the book's repository on GitHub
- [Main result: Adjoint representation of the sufficient statistic](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/results.html#adjoint_representation_of_the_sufficient_statistic): Lemma 15.1, page 206, proved. For a linear evolution equation that is diagonal in a fixed basis, the data statistic that is sufficient for the initial state is the coefficient vector of the time zero value of the solution of the backward adjoint equation driven by the data as point sources.
- [Main result: Exact sufficiency, linear case](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/results.html#exact_sufficiency_linear_case): Proposition 15.2, page 207, proved. In the linear model with a Gaussian prior the adjoint statistic is sufficient, the posterior given it is the full data posterior, and the conditional quantile map is exactly affine with slope equal to the posterior covariance.
- [Main result: Equivalence of the one step efficient score summary with the efficient centering](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/results.html#equivalence_with_the_efficient_centering): Proposition 15.5, page 210, proved. Under explicit regularity, rate and Lipschitz conditions, the cross fitted one step efficient score summary agrees with the efficient centering of Nickl's Bernstein von Mises theorem to order smaller than the root N scale in a negative Sobolev norm, so it is a computable center of the Gaussian limit of the posterior.
- [Main result: Jiang Wong under a uniform Bernstein von Mises assumption: the posterior mean summary is asymptotically sufficient](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/results.html#jiang_wong_under_bernstein_von_mises): Theorem 15.38, page 256, conditional on the uniform Bernstein von Mises assumption (Assumption U). If a Bernstein von Mises theorem holds uniformly over prior typical truths, then conditioning on the posterior mean alone, or on any summary root N equivalent to it, loses nothing at the root N scale: the recentered posterior given the summary and the recentered posterior given all of the data have the same Gaussian limit in Wasserstein distance.
- [Main result: Effective dimension under dissipation](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/results.html#effective_dimension_under_dissipation): Theorem 15.46, page 267, conditional on Assumption U and other hypotheses of the quantile generator theorem, in part (ii) for nonlinear maps. For the heat and Stokes equations on the torus with a power law prior, the number of modes in which the data at least halve the prior variance grows like a power of the sample size divided by viscosity times observation time, so dissipation lowers the effective dimension; for a nonlinear forward map, under a uniform Bernstein von Mises hypothesis and assumptions on the training residuals and the summary, a generator need only learn the posterior scale on those modes (in the linear model it needs no training), and the cost of using the prior spread beyond them is bounded explicitly.
- [Main result: Transfer of Bernstein von Mises guarantees to the GBC posterior (BvM for GBC)](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/results.html#bvm_for_gbc): Theorem 16.2, page 275, proved. If the posterior produced by a generative Bayesian computation (GBC) generator is closer to the exact posterior than the root N scale in Wasserstein distance and concentrates on the localization set with bounded moments, then it inherits the Bernstein von Mises limit of the exact posterior for the initial condition and, for the reaction diffusion and two dimensional Navier Stokes equations, for the trajectory, with exact asymptotic coverage of its credible bands and, for Navier Stokes, attainment of the local asymptotic minimax bound for bounded losses; nothing is assumed about how the generator was trained.
- [Main result: No uniform guarantee: minimax lower bound for conditional quantile generators over monotone Hölder classes](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/results.html#no_uniform_guarantee_for_quantile_generators): Theorem 16.15, page 290, proved. Any generator, trained on M simulated pairs, that must be accurate at a fixed interior summary value for every conditional law in a monotone Hölder class of conditional quantile maps of smoothness beta on a J dimensional summary has, for some map in the class, Wasserstein error at least a constant free of J times (C M) to the power minus beta over (2 beta plus J) with probability at least 1/8, where C bounds the design density, so root N accuracy uniformly over the class requires at least N to the power 1 plus J over (2 beta) simulations divided by C, more than any polynomial once J grows; reading this as the accuracy condition of the transfer theorem uses the uniform Bernstein von Mises assumption.
- [Conditional: The one step summary under four ABC criteria: Bayes risk optimal up to o(1), all four attained in the J mode Gaussian projection](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/results.html#one_step_summary_under_four_abc_criteria): Proposition 15.29, page 244, conditional on the uniform Bernstein von Mises assumption (Assumption U) and the uniform moment bound (MB)
- [Conditional: Deep PLS structure of the GBC summary](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/results.html#deep_pls_structure_of_the_gbc_summary): Proposition 15.34, page 253, conditional on the uniform Bernstein von Mises assumption (Assumption U), for the posterior given the scores alone
- [Conditional: Jiang Wong under a uniform Bernstein von Mises assumption: the posterior mean summary is asymptotically sufficient](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/results.html#jiang_wong_under_bernstein_von_mises): Theorem 15.38, page 256, conditional on the uniform Bernstein von Mises assumption (Assumption U)
- [Conditional: GBC with the posterior mean summary](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/results.html#gbc_with_the_posterior_mean_summary): Corollary 15.40, page 258, conditional on the uniform Bernstein von Mises assumption (Assumption U), for the root N statement only
- [Conditional: The Gaussian comparison models admitted by the first hypothesis of the nonlinear sufficiency gap bounds](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/results.html#sufficiency_gap_admissible_gaussian_models): Proposition 15.43, page 261, conditional on clauses (U1) and (U2) of the uniform Bernstein von Mises assumption, and (U3) for part (ii)
- [Conditional: A sufficient condition for the nonlinear sufficiency gap hypotheses in terms of the centering](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/results.html#sufficiency_gap_hypotheses_from_centering_clt): Lemma 15.44, page 263, conditional on clauses (U1) to (U3) of the uniform Bernstein von Mises assumption
- [Counterexample: A two coordinate model in which the sufficiency gap hypotheses depend on the summary](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/results.html#two_coordinate_model_sufficiency_gap_depends_on_summary): Proposition 15.45, page 264
- [Conditional: Effective dimension under dissipation](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/results.html#effective_dimension_under_dissipation): Theorem 15.46, page 267, conditional on Assumption U and other hypotheses of the quantile generator theorem, in part (ii) for nonlinear maps
- [Conditional: Sufficiency versus the raw data: simulation cost of a generator trained without a summary](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/results.html#sufficiency_versus_the_raw_data): Theorem 15.47, page 269, conditional on Assumption U and other hypotheses of the quantile generator theorem, for the second claim only
